source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Exact source records mapped to established public labels; mapping is recorded for every verse and verified against source KJV annotations. Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Jonah, Micah, and Nahum have chapter-boundary differences.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the standard commissioning opening and full parentage.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai:
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves great city and evil rising into divine presence rather than supplying the proclamation's later content.
verses.before: “Get up, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry out against it, because its evil has come up before me.”
verses.after: “Get up and go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim against it, because their evil has come up before me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry out against it, for their evil has come up before me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps all three Tarshish mentions, both presence clauses, and repeated downward motion central to the narrative.
verses.before: But Jonah got up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. He paid the fare and went down into the ship to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
verses.after: Jonah got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the LORD’s presence. He went down to Joppa, found a ship bound for Tarshish, paid its fare, and went down aboard to travel with them to Tarshish, away from the LORD’s presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jonah arose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. So he paid its fare and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Uses hurled to connect divine wind with sailors' later hurling; retains doubled great.
verses.before: But the LORD hurled a great wind onto the sea, and a great storm arose on the sea, so that the ship was about to break apart.
verses.after: But the LORD hurled a great wind onto the sea. A great storm rose on the sea, and the ship was on the point of breaking apart.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD hurled a great wind upon the sea, and there was a mighty storm upon the sea, so that the ship seemed likely to break apart.

verses.rationale: Preserves each sailor's god, cargo disposal, Jonah's further descent, and sleep contrast.
verses.before: The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his god. They threw the cargo into the sea to lighten the ship. But Jonah had gone down into the inner part of the ship, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
verses.after: The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his god. They hurled the cargo into the sea to lighten the ship. Meanwhile Jonah had gone down into the hold, lain down, and fallen fast asleep.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his god. They threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten it for them. But Jonah had gone down into the inner part of the ship and had lain down and fallen into a deep sleep.

verses.rationale: Repeats get up/call from the commission and preserves the captain's perhaps.
verses.before: The captain came to him and said, “How can you be sleeping? Get up! Call on your god. Perhaps your god will take notice of us so that we do not perish.”
verses.after: The captain came to him and said, “What are you doing asleep? Get up and call on your god! Perhaps the god will take notice of us, and we will not perish.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the captain came to him and said to him, “What are you doing, sleeper? Arise! Call upon your god. Perhaps the god will give thought to us, that we may not perish.”

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated casting and result without endorsing the procedure as generally reliable.
verses.before: Then the sailors said to one another, “Come, let us cast lots so we can learn whose fault it is that this trouble has come upon us.” They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
verses.after: The sailors said to one another, “Come, let us cast lots to find out who has brought this disaster on us.” They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they said to one another, “Come, let us cast lots, that we may know on whose account this evil has come upon us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.

verses.rationale: Preserves all five urgent questions rather than condensing the interrogation.
verses.before: They said to him, “Tell us! Who is responsible for this trouble coming upon us? What is your occupation? Where do you come from? What is your country? What people are you from?”
verses.after: They asked him, “Tell us, please, who is responsible for this disaster? What is your work? Where do you come from? What is your country? What people do you belong to?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they said to him, “Tell us, on whose account has this evil come upon us? What is your occupation? Where do you come from? What is your country? And from what people are you?”

verses.rationale: Retains fear as recurring motif and the irony of confessing the maker of the sea while fleeing across it.
verses.before: Jonah said to them, “I am a Hebrew, and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
verses.after: He answered, “I am a Hebrew. I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “I am a Hebrew, and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”

verses.rationale: Keeps intensified fear and the narrator's explanation of their knowledge.
verses.before: Then the men became terrified and said to him, “What have you done?” They knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD because he had told them.
verses.after: The men became terribly afraid and asked, “What have you done?” They knew he was fleeing from the LORD’s presence, because he had told them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the men were exceedingly afraid and said to him, “What is this that you have done?” For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.

verses.rationale: Retains the practical question and progressive storm intensity.
verses.before: They asked him, “What should we do to you so that the sea will calm down for us?” For the sea was becoming more and more stormy.
verses.after: They asked, “What should we do with you so the sea will calm down for us?” The sea was growing more and more stormy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they said to him, “What shall we do to you, that the sea may become calm for us?” For the sea was growing more and more tempestuous.

verses.rationale: Preserves Jonah's own proposed remedy and responsibility claim without inventing his motive.
verses.before: He said to them, “Pick me up and throw me into the sea, and the sea will calm down for you. I know that this great storm has come upon you because of me.”
verses.after: He told them, “Pick me up and hurl me into the sea. Then the sea will calm down for you. I know this great storm has come upon you because of me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “Take me up and throw me into the sea, and the sea will become calm for you, for I know that on my account this great storm has come upon you.”

verses.rationale: Makes their attempted alternative clear and repeats worsening sea and dry land.
verses.before: But the men rowed hard to get back to dry land, and they could not, because the sea was growing more and more stormy against them.
verses.after: Instead, the men rowed hard to get back to dry land, but they could not. The sea kept growing stormier against them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, the men rowed hard to return to dry land, but they could not, for the sea grew more and more tempestuous against them.

verses.rationale: Retains all three divine names and the sailors' explicit fear of bloodguilt.
verses.before: So they cried out to the LORD: “Please, LORD, do not let us perish because of this man’s life, and do not charge us with innocent blood. For you, LORD, have done as you pleased.”
verses.after: Then they called to the LORD: “Please, LORD, do not let us perish for this man’s life, and do not charge us with innocent blood. For you, LORD, have done as you pleased.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore they cried out to the LORD and said, “O LORD, let us not perish for this man's life, and do not place upon us innocent blood, for you, O LORD, have done as it pleased you.”

verses.rationale: Repeats the commanded action and immediate cessation without extra miraculous commentary.
verses.before: Then they picked up Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging.
verses.after: They picked Jonah up and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they took up Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its raging.

verses.rationale: Preserves fear's new object and both worship acts without relocating them to shore.
verses.before: The men feared the LORD greatly. They offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.
verses.after: Then the men feared the LORD greatly. They offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.

verses.rationale: Keeps fish unspecified, appointed as recurring verb, and exact duration; maps Hebrew2:1 to public1:17.
verses.before: The LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
verses.after: The LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

verses.rationale: Preserves setting and personal divine relationship without claiming a different fish from grammatical gender.
verses.before: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the belly of the fish,
verses.after: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the belly of the fish,

verses.rationale: Keeps past-tense thanksgiving and shift from he to you, with Sheol distinct from fish belly.
verses.before: saying, “In my distress I called to the LORD, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried for help; you heard my voice.
verses.after: He said: “In my distress I called to the LORD, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried for help, and you heard my voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “I called out to the LORD from my distress, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried for help; you heard my voice.

verses.rationale: Preserves Jonah's attribution to God and possessive your waves.
verses.before: You threw me into the deep, into the heart of the seas; the current surrounded me. All your breakers and your waves swept over me.
verses.after: You cast me into the depths, into the heart of the seas. The current surrounded me; all your breakers and waves swept over me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current surrounded me. All your breakers and your waves passed over me.

verses.rationale: Chooses yet-affirmation while noting possible question; retains temple orientation.
verses.before: Then I said, ‘I have been driven away from before your eyes; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.’
verses.after: I said, ‘I have been driven out of your sight, yet I will look again toward your holy temple.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, ‘I am driven away from before your eyes; yet I shall again look upon your holy temple.’

verses.rationale: Uses throat for nephesh in drowning context and keeps tangible weed detail.
verses.before: The waters closed over me, threatening my life; the deep surrounded me; seaweed wrapped around my head
verses.after: Water closed over me to the throat; the deep surrounded me. Seaweed was wrapped around my head.
verses.tsw_comparator: The waters closed in over me to take my life; the deep surrounded me; seaweed was wrapped around my head

verses.rationale: Preserves downward/upward reversal and ancient underworld gates without modernizing cosmology.
verses.before: at the roots of the mountains. I went down to the land whose bars closed behind me forever; yet you brought my life up from the pit, LORD my God.
verses.after: I went down to the roots of the mountains; the earth’s bars closed behind me forever. But you brought my life up from the pit, LORD my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: at the roots of the mountains. I went down to the land whose bars closed upon me forever; yet you brought up my life from the pit, O LORD my God.

verses.rationale: Keeps remembered divine name then direct address and repeated temple.
verses.before: As my life was fading away, I remembered the LORD, and my prayer came to you, into your holy temple.
verses.after: As my life was ebbing away, I remembered the LORD. My prayer came to you, into your holy temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: When my life was fainting away, I remembered the LORD, and my prayer came to you, into your holy temple.

verses.rationale: Retains ambiguous their hesed rather than deciding only grace offered them or loyalty owed.
verses.before: Those who cling to worthless idols abandon their covenant loyalty.
verses.after: Those who cling to worthless vanities abandon their faithful love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who cling to worthless idols forsake their covenant loyalty.

verses.rationale: Keeps vow/sacrifice parallels to sailors and climactic divine ownership of rescue.
verses.before: But I, with a voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to you. What I have vowed I will fulfill. Salvation belongs to the LORD.”
verses.after: But I will sacrifice to you with a voice of thanksgiving. What I have vowed, I will fulfill. Deliverance belongs to the LORD!”
verses.tsw_comparator: But I, with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to you. What I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the deliberately physical verb and dry-land motif without euphemism.
verses.before: Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.
verses.after: The LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out upon the dry land.

verses.rationale: Repeats the commission opening with explicit second chance.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the changed to-it wording and message dependence.
verses.before: “Get up, go to Nineveh, that great city, and proclaim to it the message I tell you.”
verses.after: “Get up and go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the message I give you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and proclaim to it the message that I tell you.”

verses.rationale: Retains lelohim instead of erasing God as mere intensifier and leaves journey's measurement unresolved.
verses.before: So Jonah got up and went to Nineveh according to the word of the LORD. Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, a three-day journey across.
verses.after: Jonah got up and went to Nineveh as the LORD had said. Nineveh was a city great before God, a three-day journey.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jonah arose and went to Nineveh according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, a journey of three days across.

verses.rationale: Keeps forty, one-day progress, and overturned with its destruction/transformation range.
verses.before: Jonah began to go into the city, a day's journey. He cried out: “Forty more days, and Nineveh will be overthrown.”
verses.after: Jonah began to enter the city, going a day’s journey. He proclaimed, “Forty more days, and Nineveh will be overturned!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonah began to enter the city, going a day's journey. And he cried out and said, “Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.”

verses.rationale: Preserves belief's object and social extent without inventing details of conversion.
verses.before: The people of Nineveh believed God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least.
verses.after: The people of Nineveh believed God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the people of Nineveh believed God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least of them.

verses.rationale: Keeps king of Nineveh as given and four successive abasement actions.
verses.before: When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he rose from his throne, took off his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
verses.after: When the news reached Nineveh’s king, he rose from his throne, removed his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The word reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, removed his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

verses.rationale: Retains nobles' participation and the unusual inclusion of animals in the fast.
verses.before: Then he issued a proclamation throughout Nineveh: “By decree of the king and his nobles: Neither people nor animals, herds nor flocks, are to taste anything. They must not eat or drink water.
verses.after: He had this proclamation issued in Nineveh: “By decree of the king and his nobles: No person or animal, herd or flock, may taste anything. They must not graze or drink water.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he issued a proclamation and published it throughout Nineveh: “By decree of the king and his nobles: Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything. Let them not feed or drink water.

verses.rationale: Keeps animals clothed and concrete violence as target of change rather than only ritual action.
verses.before: Let both people and animals be covered with sackcloth, and let them cry out urgently to God. Let each person turn from his evil way and from the violence in his hands.
verses.after: Let people and animals be covered with sackcloth. Let them call urgently to God. Let everyone turn from their evil way and from the violence in their hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and let them call out mightily to God. Let each turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands.

verses.rationale: Retains the uncertainty and repeated turning rather than claiming a guaranteed bargain.
verses.before: Who knows? God may turn and relent; he may turn from his burning anger, so that we do not perish.”
verses.after: Who knows? God may turn and relent, turning from his burning anger so that we do not perish.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Who knows? God may turn and relent and turn from his burning anger, so that we may not perish.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the deeds/turning basis, repeated God, and evil/disaster wordplay in contextual senses.
verses.before: God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil way. Then God relented from the disaster he had said he would bring upon them, and he did not do it.
verses.after: God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil way. God relented from the disaster he had said he would bring on them, and he did not bring it.
verses.tsw_comparator: When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil way, God relented concerning the disaster that he had said he would bring upon them, and he did not do it.

verses.rationale: Retains raah link to evil/disaster as Jonah's evaluation and heat of anger, not narrator endorsement.
verses.before: But this greatly displeased Jonah, and he became angry.
verses.after: But to Jonah this seemed a great wrong, and he burned with anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: But it was exceedingly displeasing to Jonah, and he became angry.

verses.rationale: Keeps both names, revealed flight motive, and the complete shared mercy formula as Jonah's complaint.
verses.before: He prayed to the LORD: “Please, LORD, isn't this what I said when I was still in my own land? That is why I fled to Tarshish in the first place. I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abundant in steadfast love, and one who relents from disaster.
verses.after: He prayed to the LORD: “Please, LORD, isn’t this what I said while I was still in my own country? That is why I fled toward Tarshish in the first place. I knew you were a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and rich in faithful love, who relents from bringing disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he prayed to the LORD and said, “O LORD, was not this what I said when I was still in my own land? That is why I fled beforehand to Tarshish, for I knew that you are a gracious God and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and one who relents concerning disaster.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit request for death as character speech without softening it into discouragement.
verses.before: So now, LORD, please take my life from me, because it is better for me to die than to live.”
verses.after: Now, LORD, please take my life from me. I would be better off dead than alive.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore now, O LORD, please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.”

verses.rationale: Retains the evaluative question with intensity alternative noted.
verses.before: The LORD said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
verses.after: The LORD asked, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”

verses.rationale: Keeps east, shelter, shade, and waiting without rearranging chronology.
verses.before: Jonah went out of the city and sat down east of the city. He made a shelter for himself there and sat under it in the shade, waiting to see what would happen to the city.
verses.after: Jonah went out of the city and sat to its east. He made himself a shelter there and sat in its shade to see what would happen to the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jonah went out of the city and sat to the east of the city. There he made a shelter for himself and sat under it in the shade, until he might see what would become of the city.

verses.rationale: Preserves combined divine title, appointed motif, and great delight contrasting great wrong; species left unspecified.
verses.before: The LORD God appointed a plant and made it grow over Jonah to provide shade for his head and relieve his discomfort. Jonah was delighted with the plant.
verses.after: The LORD God appointed a plant, which grew up over Jonah to shade his head and relieve his distress. Jonah was greatly delighted with the plant.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD God appointed a plant and caused it to grow up over Jonah, to provide shade for his head, to deliver him from his discomfort. So Jonah rejoiced greatly because of the plant.

verses.rationale: Keeps timing, repeated appointed, and causal plant death.
verses.before: But at dawn the next day, God appointed a worm, and it attacked the plant so that it withered.
verses.after: At dawn the next day, God appointed a worm. It attacked the plant, and the plant withered.
verses.tsw_comparator: But God appointed a worm when dawn came the next day, and it attacked the plant so that it withered.

verses.rationale: Preserves appointed third agent and repeated death speech; rare wind adjective noted.
verses.before: When the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind. The sun beat down on Jonah's head until he grew faint. He asked to die and said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
verses.after: When the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind. The sun beat down on Jonah’s head until he grew faint. He asked to die, saying, “I would be better off dead than alive.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun beat down upon Jonah's head so that he grew faint. And he asked that he might die and said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”

verses.rationale: Repeats the evaluative question and Jonah's intensified self-justification.
verses.before: God said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?” Jonah said, “It is right for me to be angry— angry enough to die.”
verses.after: God asked Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?” He answered, “It is right for me to be angry—angry enough to die!”
verses.tsw_comparator: But God said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?” And he said, “It is right for me to be angry, angry enough to die.”

verses.rationale: Keeps compassion and repeated overnight brevity as the comparison's grounds.
verses.before: Then the LORD said, “You had compassion on the plant, though you did not labor for it or make it grow. It came up in a night and perished in a night.
verses.after: The LORD said, “You have compassion for the plant, though you did not labor over it or make it grow. It came into being in a night and perished in a night.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said, “You had compassion on the plant, for which you did not labor, nor did you make it grow, which came into being in a night and perished in a night.

verses.rationale: Preserves the open final question, more-than count, unresolved right/left idiom, and final animals.
verses.before: Should I not have compassion on Nineveh, that great city, where there are more than one hundred twenty thousand people who do not know their right hand from their left— and many animals besides?”
verses.after: Should I not have compassion for Nineveh, the great city, with more than 120,000 people who cannot distinguish their right hand from their left—and many animals?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And should I not have compassion on Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than one hundred twenty thousand persons who do not know their right hand from their left, and also many animals?”

comparative_references.scope: All 48 TSW verses bound and compared programmatically after independent drafting from each selected original-language record and all annotations. Selected differences read during focused authoring checks. Overlap is triage only.
